ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To kill without blinking describes ruthless, unhindered action. In Chan records it is joined—often in the same sentence—to becoming buddha on the spot, so the violent idiom serves as a public measure of complete decisiveness rather than a report of homicide.
EvidenceBody: Mingyin rejects common explanations of Guang'e the butcher with the phrase; Yuanwu joins the person who kills without blinking to one who becomes buddha immediately; Yunju Liaoyuan applies it to a general, while Cao Han names himself a general who kills without blinking and is answered by Longshou Wuyi.
